summary: Preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executes heavily obfuscated sibling payload via Bun
details: @onereach/content-builder-template-compiler@0.0.5 declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs' in package.json. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<arch>.zip (or uses a pre-existing bun) and invokes it via execFileSync against a bundled sibling file, math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line file using hex-mangled identifiers, a shuffled string-array cipher (WV8StW rotating via push/shift), a ~1500-entry constant table, and 'with' statements — canonical obfuscator.io-style transforms — and is prefixed '// @bun @bun-cjs' so it only runs under Bun. The package advertises itself as a small template compiler whose only legitimate dependency need is lodash; there is no engineering reason to fetch a full alternate JavaScript runtime and execute an obfuscated 727KB blob under it at install time. The alternate-runtime shape shifts execution off the Node interpreter that most scanners inspect, and the obfuscation conceals the payload's actual behavior. Installing this package causes the obfuscated payload to run on the installer's machine before any user code executes.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
